defaults.permitted_development: Across Greater London, a side extension normally only falls within Class A if it is single storey, stays behind the principal elevation and does not exceed half the width of the original house. rules.height_rules: Across Greater London, the usual side-extension fallback is an overall height of up to 4m, with eaves at or below 3m where any part sits within 2m of a boundary. Keeping the side roof low is usually what stops the flank wall becoming visually heavy.
rules.depth_rules: There is no separate side-extension depth allowance in the way people often expect. The real test is whether the addition stays clearly subordinate to the original house and does not turn the side elevation into an oversized new wing.
rules.boundary_rules: Across Greater London, the key boundary checks are width, side-gap character, neighbour outlook and whether the addition creates an overbearing flank wall from the street or adjoining land.
rules.roof_rules: Keep the roof clearly secondary to the main house. A simple, low side roof is usually easier to defend than a taller form that competes with the original ridgeline.
rules.materials_rules: Materials should match or sit very closely with the existing house so the side addition reads as part of the dwelling rather than a bolt-on block.
